instruction: Georeferenced Office IFC CSV Area Schedule This task starts from scratch. No local reference images are provided. Create a georeferenced one-storey office layout, save the model as result.ifc, and use Bonsai/IfcCSV-style IFC data export to save the space area schedule as result.csv. 1. The output folder contains these files with exact relative paths: result.ifc, result.csv. 2. Result.ifc is an IFC4 model with exactly one IfcProject, exactly one IfcBuildingStorey named Level 00, and zero IfcBuildingElementProxy elements. 3. The model contains exactly three IfcSpace elements named Office, Meeting, and WC after case, hyphen, and underscore normalization. 4. The spaces have Qto_SpaceBaseQuantities NetFloorArea values within 0.05 m2 of these targets: Office: 28.00, Meeting: 8.58, WC: 3.90. 5. The model contains exactly six IfcWall elements named South Wall, East Wall, North Wall, West Wall, Meeting Partition, and WC Partition, and exactly one IfcSlab named Office Slab. 6. The combined geometric bounding box of the six walls and the slab spans 9.00 m in X, 6.00 m in Y, and 3.00 m in Z, each within 0.05 m. 7. The model contains exactly one IfcProjectedCRS with Name EPSG:3857, MapProjection Pseudo-Mercator, and MapZone Zone-Local. 8. The model contains exactly one IfcMapConversion with Eastings 498765.00, Northings 6812345.00, OrthogonalHeight 35.00, XAxisAbscissa 1.00, XAxisOrdinate 0.00, and Scale 1.00, each within 0.01. 9. Result.csv has this exact header order after trimming whitespace: SpaceName, Level, NetFloorArea. 10. Result.csv has exactly three non-empty data rows for Office, Meeting, and WC; every row has Level equal to Level 00, and each NetFloorArea value matches the corresponding IFC NetFloorArea within 0.05 m2. Any item not explicitly required may vary.
